resolved.explanation: The passage says the easing to about 2 percent reflects the early-2026 tariff cut after the Supreme Court ruling, and the edge up comes mainly from the Canadian tariffs; without that, a viewer placed right after s16's 'one-time bump or lasting inflation?' can read the easing as prices drifting back on their own. resolved.suggestion: Say 'peaked near 3 percent in February 2026, is forecast to ease to about 2 percent by August after a court ruling cut some tariffs, then edge up again with new tariffs on Canadian goods.'

resolved.explanation: Straight after s07-s08 (94 and 86 percent stay with importers), '26 percent passes through to consumer prices' invites the reading that importers and shops swallowed the other three quarters. The corpus explains most of the gap differently: distribution margins are about half of what consumers pay, and imports are only part of consumer goods (Oct 2026 post, L13-L16), but that passage is not cited and the script leaves the gap unexplained.
resolved.suggestion: Either rephrase so it does not read as a share of the importer's cost ('consumer goods prices rise by about a quarter of the tariff rate'), or set generation.needsEvidence for the distribution-margin passage and add a short clause on why the shelf share is smaller than the border share.
